==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:score|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|score}}, {{m|enm|skore}}, {{m|enm|schore}}, from {{inh|en|ang|scoru||notch; tally; score}}, from {{der|en|non|skor}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skurō||incision; tear; rift}}, which is related to {{m|gem-pro|*skeraną||to cut}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-||cut}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|skora}}, {{cog|sv|skåra}}, {{cog|da|skår}}. Related to {{m|en|shear}}. For the sense “twenty”: The mark on a tally made by [[drover|drovers]] for every twenty beasts passing through a [[tollgate]]. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|skôr|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/skɔː/}} * {{enPR|skôrʹ|a=GenAm}}, {{IPA|en|/skoɹ/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-score.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/skoː/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{enPR|skōrʹ|a=rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}, {{IPA|en|/sko(ː)ɹ/}} * {{IPA|en|/skoə/|a=non-rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)|s=1}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|s|*}} {{number box|en|20}} # {{senseid|en|number of points}} The total number of goals, [[point]]s, [[run]]s, etc. earned by a [[participant]] in a [[game]]. #: {{ux|en|The player with the highest '''score''' is the winner.}} # The number of points [[accrue]]d by each of the participants in a [[game]], expressed as a [[ratio]] or a series of numbers. #: {{ux|en|The '''score''' is 8-1 even though it's not even half-time!}} # The performance of an individual or group on an examination or test, expressed by a number, letter, or other symbol; a [[grade]]. #: {{ux|en|The test '''scores''' for this class were high.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Rory Smith|title=IQ scores are falling and have been for decades, new study finds|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/13/health/falling-iq-scores-study-intl|date=2018-06-13|passage=The study not only showed IQ variance between children the same parents, but because the authors had the IQ '''scores''' of various parents, it demonstrated that parents with higher IQs tended to have more kids, ruling out the dysgenic fertility theory as a driver of falling IQ '''scores''' and highlighting the role of environmental factors instead.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260402133215/https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/13/health/falling-iq-scores-study-intl|archivedate=2 April 2026}} # {{senseid|en|Q40292}} {{U|twenty}} ({{l|mul|20}}). #* {{RQ:Lincoln Gettysburg|Bliss|1|passage=Four '''score''' and seven years ago our fathers brought forth, on this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.}} ## A [[distance]] of twenty [[yard]]s, in ancient [[archery]] and [[gunnery]]. ##* {{RQ:Drayton Poly-Olbion|26|passage=At Markes full fortie '''score''' they vs'd to Prick and Roue.}} ## A [[weight]] of twenty [[pound]]s. ## A [[period]] of twenty [[year]]s. ## {{lb|en|Britain|slang}} Twenty [[pounds sterling]]. ##* {{quote-song|en|date=2012-09-09|artist={{w|Plan B (musician)|Plan B}},Chip,Devlin|title=Deepest Shame (New Machine Remix)|passage=DEVLIN:You know the apple and core. Head might cost you a '''score''', or more if you want a meat show on all fours.}} # {{lb|en|often in the plural}} A [[great deal]]; [[many]], [[several]]. #: {{ux|en|Some words have '''scores''' of meanings.}} # {{lb|en|gambling}} An [[amount]] of [[money]] won in [[gambling]]; [[winning]]s. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Arnold Snyder|title=Big Book of Blackjack |passage=Use a few “introductory plays” to become known to a casino before you go for a big '''score'''.}} # {{senseid|en|music}}{{lb|en|music}} The written form of a [[musical]] [[composition]] showing all instrumental and vocal parts. # {{lb|en|music}} The music of a [[movie]] or [[play]]. #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=55| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/21580191-edward-snowdens-odyssey-leaves-america-nonplussed-and-its-allies-dismayed-russia-china Travels and travails]| passage=Even without hovering drones, a lurking assassin, a thumping '''score''' and a denouement, the real-life story of Edward Snowden, a rogue spy on the run, could be straight out of the cinema. But, as with Hollywood, the subplots and exotic locations may distract from the real message: America’s discomfort and its foes’ glee.}} # A [[subject]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=w:Plato|title=Sophist|translator=Lesley Brown|page=245e |passage=Well, although we haven't discussed the views of all those who make precise reckonings of being and not [being], we've done enough on that '''score'''.}} # An [[account]]; a [[reason]]; a [[motive]]; a [[sake]]; a [[behalf]]. #* {{RQ:Butler Hudibras |year=1905|passage=But left the trade, as many more / Have lately done on the same '''score'''.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Indian Emperour|page=65|passage=You act your kindneſs on ''Cydaria''’s '''ſcore'''.}} # A [[notch]] or [[incision]]; especially, one that is made as a tally mark; hence, a mark, or line, made for the purpose of account. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|IV|vii|passage=Whereas, before, our forefathers had no other books but the '''score''' and the tally, thou hast caused printing to be used.}} # An account or reckoning; account of dues; bill; [[debt]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Macbeth|V|viii|passage=He parted well, and paid his '''score'''.}} # {{lb|en|US|slang|crime}} A [[criminal]] [[act]], especially: ## A [[robbery]]. ##: {{ux|en|Let's pull a '''score'''!}} ##* {{quote-av|en|writers=Matt Reeves; Peter Craig|title={{w|The Batman (film)|The Batman}}|year=2022|passage=Batman: Dangerous crowd you're stealing from.
Catwoman: Jesus. Is this how you get your kicks, hon? Sneaking up on girls in the dark?
Batman: Is that why you work in the club? It was all just a '''score'''?}} ## A [[bribe]] paid to a [[police officer]]. ## An illegal [[sale]], especially of [[drugs]]. ##: {{ux|en|He made a big '''score'''.}} ## A [[prostitute]]'s [[client]]. # {{lb|en|originally|US|vulgar|slang}} A [[sexual]] [[conquest]]. # {{lb|en|UK|regional}} In the [[Lowestoft]] area, a [[narrow]] [[pathway]] running down a [[cliff]] to the [[beach]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1975|author=John Seymour|title=The Companion Guide to the Coast of North-east England|page=206 |passage=Above the harbour, steeply up the hill, run The Bolts, narrow stepped passages, equivalent of The '''Scores''' of Lowestoft and The Rows of Great Yarmouth.}} # A document which systematically lists differences among compiled manuscripts of a source text. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Daniel E. Fleming and Sara J. Milstein|title=The Buried Foundation of the Gilgamesh Epic|page=8 |passage=Robson counted 92 exemplars of Gilgamesh and Huwawa A and 59 of Gilgamesh, Enkidu, and the Netherworld (“Tablet House,” 54). Since that time, several joins have reduced the number of distinct copies, so that Delnero’s '''score''' for Gilgamesh and Huwawa A now includes 85 total, mostly of the Type III extract category (Variation in Sumerian Literary Compositions: A Case Study Based on the Decad, University of Pennsylvania Ph.D., 2006).}} ====Usage notes==== * As a quantity, a score is counted as any other unit: ''ten score'', ''twelve score'', ''fourteen score'', etc. (or ''[[tenscore]]'', ''[[twelvescore]]''). After all, I've '''scored''' by it."}} ## To [[earn]] [[point]]s in a [[game]]. ##: {{ux|en|It is unusual for a team to '''score''' a hundred goals in one game.}} ##: {{ux|en|Pelé '''scores''' again!}} ## To [[achieve]] academic credit on a test, quiz, homework, assignment, or course. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Diane McGuinness|title=Early reading instruction: what science really tells us about how to teach reading |passage=At the end of first grade, the children '''scored''' 80 percent correct on this test, a value that remained unchanged through third grade.}} ##* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Rory Smith|title=IQ scores are falling and have been for decades, new study finds|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/13/health/falling-iq-scores-study-intl|date=2018-06-13|passage=Intelligence is heritable, and for a long time, researchers assumed that people with high IQ scores would have kids who also '''scored''' above average.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260402133215/https://www.cnn.com/2018/06/13/health/falling-iq-scores-study-intl|archivedate=2 April 2026}} ## {{lb|en|gambling}} To win money by gambling. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Shannon Nash|title=For the Love of Money|page=215 |passage={{...}} he '''scored''' big by hitting the jack pot at the Bellagio (he won $7,000).
